message.content:
**Quick note:**  
`docker start <container>` is used to start **containers**, not the Docker daemon itself.  
To bring up the Docker Engine (the background service that runs containers) on Windows you need to start the *Docker Desktop* service (or the legacy `com.docker.service` if you’re still using Docker Toolbox).

---

### Starting Docker Desktop from PowerShell

```powershell
# Start the Docker Desktop service (requires administrative rights)
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

If you prefer the classic `sc` command:

```cmd
sc start com.docker.service
```

> **Tip:** If you’re running Docker Desktop as a normal user, you can simply launch the Docker Desktop app from the Start menu – it will automatically start the underlying service.

---

### Checking status

```powershell
Get-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

You should see `Status : Running` once the service has started.

---

### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| “Access denied” when running `Start-Service` | Run PowerShell as Administrator |
| Service name not found | Verify Docker Desktop is installed (`C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker`) |
| Docker Desktop still shows “Not running” after starting service | Restart your computer or reinstall Docker Desktop |

---

#### One‑liner you can paste into a `.bat` file

```bat
@echo off
powershell -NoProfile -Command "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service"
```

Save that as `start-docker.bat`, double‑click it (right‑click → Run as administrator), and Docker should come online.

Let me know if you hit any errors or need help troubleshooting!
